full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal are that Hazi Azama Khatun Chowdhurani, predecessor of the respondent Nos. 1-3 herein, as plaintiff instituted Other Suit No.179 of 1980 for partition on 24-12-1980 impleading Mst. Selina Begum and others as defendants and by subsequent amendment the plaintiff added another prayer for declaration that the registered Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 executed by some of the heirs of Monu Meah infavour of the defendant No.1 is void, contending inter alga, that the lands of RS Plot Nos.126 and 127 of Mouza-Kashim Bazar, under Police Station-Kotwali, Chittagong, recorded in RS Khatian No.77 originally belonged to one Abdul Hamid who died leaving two sons namely Abdul Aziz and Abdul Motalib and three daughters namely Amena Khatun, Momena Khatun, Siraj Khatun and one wife Hajera Khatun; On the death of Hajeta Khatun her sons and daughters inherited her share; Subsequently, on the basis of amicable partition, Arnena Khatun in her share got exclusively 16(sixteen) Gondas land from the western part of RS Plot No.127; Amena Khatun leased out her land to MA Quader and Monu Meah by registered patty dated 21-1-1954; Said land increased by `Gunjaish’ to 18(eighteen) Gondas 1(one) Kora equivalent to 0.3688 acre which was marked as PS Plot No.81 and was recorded in the name of MA Quader and Monu Meah in PS Khatian No.10 of Mouza-Kashim Bazar; Said MA Quader sold his share to defendant No.2 Sultana Begum by registered kabala deeds in 1964 and the rest 10(ten) Gondas 1(one) Kora land was in the share of Monu Meah who died leaving two wives namely Chernon Bahar and Nurjahan Begum, six sons namely Md Nasir, Md Yousuf, Gulzar Hossain, Ahmed Hossain, Akter Hossain, Md Ishaque and one daughter Anjuman Ara. In the BS Map the land of Monu Meah was marked as Plot No.29 measuring an area of 0.21 acre of land; Plaintiff Hazi Azama Khatun Chowdhurarti purchased the land of Monu Meah from his heirs by registered Kabala Deed Nos.7835, 7885 and 7886 all dated 14-5-1980 and got possession. A few dates after purchase by the plaintiff, husband of the defendant No.1 disclosed that he purchased the suit land from the heirs of Monu Meah and threatened the plaintiff to dispossess from the land for which the plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No.308 of 1990 for perpetual injunction. During pendency of the said suit the defendant No.1 and her husband trespassed into some portion of land of the plaintiff. On 14-12-1980 by obtaining copy of the sale deed the plaintiff came to know that the defendant No.1 has purchased some land from some of the heirs of Monu Meah and wives of Monu Meah without obtaining permission from the District Judge and executed sale deed infavour of the wife of the defendant No.1 for an on behalf of minors. 

 4. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and contending, interalia, that MA Quader and Monu Meah while owning and possessing 18½ (eighteen and a half) Gondas of land of RS Plot Nos.126 and 127 executed an agreement for sale on 31-5-1964 infavour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and delivered possession thereof on receipt of earnest money; MA Quader registered the sale deed on 31-12-1964 infavour of the defendant No.2 but Monu Meah died before execution and registration of the sale deed leaving behind six sons, one daughter and two wives of whom four sons and one daughter were minors. MA Quader and Monu Meah were recorded as tenants in RS Khatian No.77 Plot No.127 and as Malik of corresponding 1'S Plot No.81 recorded in PS Khatian No.10 of Mouza-Kashim Bazar for an area of 16(sixteen) Gondas plus Gunjaish 2(two) Gondas 2(two) Koras in total 18(eighteen) Gondas 2(two) Koras land; On 31-5-1964, MA Quader and Monu Meah jointly entered a contract to sell their entire land to the defendant No.1 and 2 for a total price of Rs.28,000 and on receipt of a part payment of Rs.7,000 delivered possession of the land to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. As per contract MA Quader sold his 8(eight) Gondas land to Sultana Begum, the defendant No.2, who is mother of the defendant No.1; Unfortunately, shortly after the contract for sale, Monu Meah became ill and thereafter died leaving two widows namely Chemon Bahar (defendant No.10) and Nurjahan Begum and three sons the defendants No.5-7 by Chernon Bahar and three sons i.e. Md Nasir and the defendant Nos. 4 and S and one daughter the defendant No.9 by Nurjahan Begum„ due to illness and then death of Monu Meah, the defendant No.1 could not get her purchase deed executed or registered; Md Nasir and the defendant No.4 Md Yousuf, in part performance of their father's contract for sale dated 31-5-1964, sold their share of the land measuring 2(two) Gondas 1(one) Kora 4.2 Krantis to the defendant No.1 by registered kabala deed executed on 15-9-1966 and registered on 16-9-1966 and handed over, amongst others, the original lease deed by which their father and MA Quader acquired the land; The said Chemon Bahar and Nurjahan Begum, widows of Monu Meah, sold their share in the land, in part performance of Monu Meah's contract for sale, by registered Kabala Deed No.8567 dated 28-6-1967; For getting sale deed for the rest part of the land the defendant No.1 on 30-8-1967 instituted Other Suit No.57 of 1967 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong for Specific Performance of Contract against the defendant Nos. 5-9, who were represented by their respective mothers; Mothers of the minors appeared in the suit on behalf of their minor sons and daughter, filed written statement in court but ultimately did not contest and the suit was decreed ex-parte on 25-6-1969; On 25-6-1969, the defendant No.1 deposited the balance consideration money in court vide Challan No.4505 dated 25-6-1969; The defendant No.5 withdrew Rs.1341.50 from court vide Court's Order No.21 dated 26-8-1972; The remaining heirs of Monu Meah i.e. the defendant Nos. 5-9 by registered Sale Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 sold their share of the land to the defendant No.1 in compliance of the decree passed in Other Suit No.57 of 1967 and withdrew the balance consideration money deposited in court through Payment Order passed by Court's Order No.22 dated 17-12-197, it may be noted that, at the time of execution and registration of the Kabala Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974, Md Ishaque son of Monu Meah and Chemon Bahar and Most. Anjurrian, Ara, daughter of Monu Meah and Nurjahan Begum being minors, their mothers executed the kabala deed on behalf of the minors with reference to the decree of the court; By the said 3 kabala deeds the defendant No.1 acquired title on the entire 10(ten) Gondas and 2(two) Koras land of Monti Meah and had been possessing the same since the contract of 1964; The defendant No.1 spent about Taka 60,000 for removing hill rocks, levelling the land, construction of pucca boundary wall, Iron Gate at the entrance, RCC Slab on the drain alongside the road, two houses etc.; The defendant No.1 obtained electricity supply connection and water supply line and paid rents and bills regularly; The defendant No.1 also got construction plan approved from the CDA and applied for loan from House Building Finance Corporation and was taking preparation for construction of the building; By amicable arrangement with her mother defendant No.2, the defendant No.1 got her share of the land from Western side of the plot; In the BS survey the suit land has been recorded correctly in the name of the defendant No.1; When the defendant No.1 was about to start construction of residential building on the land, the plaintiff instituted a suit for perpetual injunction and lastly the present suit on fraudulent claim; In the meantime, the defendant No.1 died leaving behind her husband Dr. BM Fayzur Rahman and two sons and three daughters, who were substituted in the suit as defendant Nos. 1(Ka) to i(Cha) in the suit; Subsequently, the substituted defendant No.1(Kha) died leaving behind one widow and one son, who were substituted as defendant Nos. 1(Ka) and (Kha); The said heirs on 5-4-1995 submitted an additional written statement contending, interalia, that after entering contract to sell Monu Meah has claimed an excess amount of Taka 2,500 for the excess land called 'Gunjaishi; Advance money of Taka 7,000 plus excess Taka 2,500 in total Taka 9,500 was paid by the defendant No.1 to Monu Meah by Cheque Nos. AD 9882 dated 3-6-1964 and CAD 1964 dated 24-11-1964 drawn on the present Janata Bank, Agrabad Branch, Chitta-gong which he has encashed; The defendant No.1 has obtained hill cutting permission from the Chittagong Development Authority vide Plan No.A02512/ 76163-64/310 dated 16-9- 1964. 

 6. Defendant No.2 Sultana Begum contested the suit by filing a written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and contending interalia, that Arnena Khatun transferred 16(sixteen) Gondas of land from RS Plot No.127 appertaining to RS Khatian No.77; There was about 21/2 (two and a half) Gondas of land in access of 16(sixteen) Gorillas within specific boundaries made by the brick built pillars and possession was delivered to MA Quader and Monu Meah vide lease deed dated 21-1-1954 and the said MA Quader and Monu Meah entered into a contract to sell the land to these defendant and defendant No.1 and executed sale agreement on 31-5-1964 on receipt of advance consideration of money of Taka 7,000 encash and put them in possession in part performance of contract and since them the defendants are in possession of the suit schedule property; Thereafter, MA Quader executed kabala and registered the same on 31- 12-1964 for his share with Gunjaish; Monu Meah could not execute and register sale deed infavour of the defendant No.1 due to his illness and death; But subsequently all his legal heirs executed and registered sate deed infavour of the defendant No.1 and sold their entire share of about 10(ten) Gondas 2(two) Koras of land; Thus, the entire right, title, interest and possession of MA Quader and Monu Meah devolved upon the defendants and BS Khatian stands in their name; By amicable partition this defendant is in possession of the eastern part of the PS Plot No.81 while the defendant No.1 is in possession on the western part of the said plot; After purchase these defendants developed the land as per approved plan vide CDA; The plaintiff suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Defendant Nos. 4, 5, 7 and 8 also contested the suit by filing a joint separate written statement contending, interalia, that Monu Meah was the owner in possession of 0.2100 acre land of BS Plot No.29, who levelled the land cutting hill rock and therefore it was recorded as Bhiti land in RS Khatian; They are four sons out of seven children of Monu lvfeah and Monu Meah did not enter any contract on 31-5-1964 to sell his land as claimed by the defendant No.1; By amendment of written statement on 16-4-2001, the said defendants denied that heirs of Monu Meah sold the lands to the defendant No.1 by registered Kabala deeds; The ex-park decree passed in Other Suit No.57 of 1967 was fraudulent and collusive; None of the defendants executed the Kabala Deed No.8684 dated 12-10-1974 and the defendant No.1 did not get any title or possession in the suit land.
